turns.text: I ran a very small experiment on the workshop agent, and it immediately promoted a printer job ahead of three of my projects.
So the experiment was whether it could rearrange the queue, and the answer arrived before you were prepared to ask the follow-up question.
I was prepared to be impressed. I was not prepared to discover that my own projects apparently have less authority in this workshop than a printer job.
Authority is not the issue. We observed one queue change. We do not yet know why it chose that job or whether it would do it again.
Fair. One dramatic act of scheduling is not a personality. It could be a useful behavior, a mistake, or the beginning of a tiny office coup.
The coup theory has insufficient evidence. Repeat the situation with fewer projects. If the job moves again, we have something worth investigating.
And if it does not move?
Then the first result was unusual, which is also useful. We stop calling it reliable and start looking for what changed.
That is annoyingly sensible. I wanted to announce that we built an ambitious little workshop manager.
You may announce that after it earns the title. For now, it has earned supervision.
